strategy.arms.aria: {game}: profit and loss distribution for three methods
strategy.arms.conclusion.blackjack: Basic strategy keeps losses smallest, but the average is still below zero. In a very long measurement, the house edge under basic strategy is {edge}, and the average of a {n}-round simulation swings by about plus or minus {ci} by chance.
strategy.arms.conclusion.crash: In theory the expected value of all three methods is the same. Small differences in the table are simulation error; what changes is the width of the distribution.
strategy.arms.conclusion.roulette: In theory the expected value of all three methods is the same. Small differences in the table are simulation error; what changes is the width of the distribution.
strategy.arms.def.blackjack: My strategy: the recorded frequency of actions by situation is reused (basic strategy for situations not seen before). Random: any one of the possible actions. Optimal: basic strategy.
strategy.arms.def.crash: My strategy: the multiplier you actually aimed for is drawn again and used. Random: any target between {min} and {max}. Optimal: since every target has the same expected value, {min}, which swings the result least.
strategy.arms.def.roulette: My strategy: the placements you actually made are drawn again and used. Random: one square chosen at random among the possible single bets. Optimal: since every placement has the same expected value, one red square, which swings the result least.
strategy.arms.lead: All three methods played {n} rounds each, over the same sequence of cards, numbers and multipliers. The chart shows how the net spreads when grouped into blocks the length of your session ({block} rounds).
strategy.arms.title: My strategy against random and optimal
strategy.arms.x: Horizontal: net over {block} rounds (credits, based on an average bet of {bet}) · vertical: share of results
strategy.arms.xUnits: Horizontal: net over {block} rounds (bet units) · vertical: share of results
strategy.bj.devTitle: Decisions that cost the most expected value
strategy.bj.evNote: The expected value lost is an approximation, calculated as if the deck were infinite. It has no bearing on whether that round's result was actually good or bad.
strategy.bj.lead: Basic strategy is a table of the action with the highest expected value in each situation (your hand, and the card the dealer shows). Your decisions were compared with that table.
strategy.bj.noDecisions: There were no rounds with a decision to make. Even if basic strategy is followed, a house edge of {edge} remains.
strategy.bj.perfect: All {decisions} decisions matched basic strategy. A house edge of {edge} still remains.
strategy.bj.summary: Of {decisions} decisions, {matches} matched basic strategy. The {dev} deviations cost about {loss} credits of expected value. Even if basic strategy had been followed exactly, a house edge of {edge} would remain.
strategy.bj.unresolved: {n} decisions that could not be reconstructed from the record were left out of the count.
strategy.cr.actual: The actual return rate in this session was {actual}. With few rounds, this value can deviate greatly from {rtp} because of luck.
strategy.cr.lead: In Crash, whichever target multiplier is chosen, and whenever you cash out yourself, the long-run return rate is the same at {rtp}. High targets pay rarely and by a lot; low targets pay often and by a little.
strategy.cr.targetsLead: The same {n} crash points were given several target multipliers, applied equally.
strategy.cr.targetsNote: The higher the target, the rarer the success, so the simulated value swings more. The calculated value is nearly the same whatever the target.
strategy.lead: This shows how much the choices made in each game changed the result. Blackjack is the only game where choices change the expected value, and even there the best choices only reduce the loss; they do not remove it. In the other games, choices only change how widely the results swing.
strategy.noStrategy.ocean: Abyss Legend: neither staying at the seat after an omen nor the operations in between change the probability. The long-run return rate is {rtp}.
strategy.noStrategy.slot: Slot: the timing of the spin, the STOP button, swipes and bet size do not change the chance of winning. The long-run return rate is {rtp}.
strategy.noStrategy.title: Games without choices
strategy.none: In this session there were no games (Blackjack, Roulette, Crash) in which choices affected the result.
strategy.rl.lead: Roulette numbers are decided fresh every time. Whichever square you bet on, and whatever you do based on the previous result, the expected value of one round is a loss of {edge} of the amount wagered.
strategy.rl.martingale.no: No Martingale pattern (doubling the bet after a loss) was seen. Rounds in which the bet was raised to about double right after a loss: {n}.
strategy.rl.martingale.why: Doubling wins small amounts often, but a losing streak causes a large loss all at once. The expected value stays the same.
strategy.rl.martingale.yes: Martingale pattern: there were {n} rounds in which the bet was raised to about double right after a loss (longest run: {len} in a row; maximum bet: {max} credits).
strategy.rl.streak: There were {opps} rounds right after the same colour came up {k} or more times in a row. In those rounds, {against} bets were placed on the opposite colour and {with} on the same colour.
strategy.rl.streak.none: There was no round right after the same colour came up {k} or more times in a row.
strategy.rl.streak.why: The thought that it is now the other colour's turn is the gambler's fallacy. The wheel does not remember the previous result.
strategy.rl.unchanged: Betting patterns only change the order of wins and losses and how much is lost at a time; they do not change the expected value.
strategy.scaled: On this device the calculation was reduced, and it ran for {n} rounds (originally {requested} rounds).
